items.title: Carl Rinker Interview, 1962-10-14
items.q: And shortly after that I met the Bruny's boys Merritt, Henry, and George

ctx.x: My name is Carl Rinker and I play trumpet. I played in Chicago from starting about 1924 until roughly about 1939 when I discontinued trumpet playing to go into other work.

During that time I played with many musicians from New Orleans. I believe the first one I met was Rag Baby Stevens, drummer. That was when I was playing out on Milwaukee Avenue about the first job I ever played. A place called the House of Niles. I think I met Larry Shields there also. Shortly after that I played at a place on West Madison Street owned by Tommy Thomas in which Ray Bozeman was the saxophone clarinet player and he was a very excellent one. And shortly after that I met the Bruny's boys Merritt,…

talking with uh Bill about his uh uh year, Carl really, in talking to Carl about his years in uh Chicago Jazz I discovered that he crossed lines frequently and so on the uh 16th of uh October 1962 I asked him to put down a few comments on tape on some of these uh people that he had mentioned as we went over the interview. Uh I thought that many of his comments about their playing quality was interesting. What did you think of uh Bouchon as a uh baritone player? I could say he was the greatest
